title: Finance as a Service (FaaS): What It Is and How to Choose a Provider
summary: Finance as a Service (FaaS) is one team running a company's whole finance function, bookkeeping through CFO advice, under one engagement. What it includes, how it compares to an accounting firm or in-house team, who it fits, and how to choose a provider.
body_markdown:
What does a Finance as a Service engagement include?


Four layers owned by one team: bookkeeping, GAAP accounting and the monthly close, tax compliance and planning, and CFO-level advisory with FP&A. A single team runs all four from the same books, so the close, the return and the forecast tie to the same numbers. Payroll, R&D tax credits and 409A valuations are added when the company needs them.


Is Finance as a Service the same as outsourced accounting?


No. A traditional outsourced accounting firm keeps the books or files the return, usually in separate departments that hand work between them. Finance as a Service covers the whole function, from bookkeeping through CFO advice, under one accountable team, so there is no gap between the people closing the books and the people reading them.


How is FaaS different from a fractional CFO?


FaaS includes one. A standalone fractional CFO provides strategy and reporting without the bookkeeping and close beneath it, advising on numbers someone else produced. In Finance as a Service the CFO layer sits on top of books the same team closed every month.


What size company is a good fit?


The model fits from a first raise through $30M in revenue and beyond, for venture-backed, bootstrapped and PE-backed companies. Very early, a founder and a bookkeeper may be enough. The bundle starts paying for itself when the layers depend on each other: a first board package, an audit request, a priced round, or a second entity or state.


Can Finance as a Service replace an in-house finance team?


For most companies up to about $30M, yes. It covers what a bookkeeper, accountant, controller and fractional CFO would, without the fixed headcount. Building the first three of those roles in-house runs past $350,000 a year on BLS median wages before any CFO capacity. Past $30M, some roles often move in-house, with the engagement shifting to consolidation, audit and technical accounting.


How is Finance as a Service priced?


On a monthly fee that depends on transaction volume, stage, entity count and the services you choose, usually on month-to-month terms. indinero quotes per engagement after a scoping call; starting points are on the Pricing page.


How quickly can a provider take over the books?


It depends on the condition of the records. Current, reconciled books transfer in weeks; a backlog is cleaned up first. indinero reconciles prior periods, runs one close in parallel with your current setup, then takes over. Average onboarding is 18 days.


Does "Finance as a Service" mean embedded banking or payments?


In fintech, the same phrase is sometimes used for banking, payments and lending delivered through APIs. In accounting, and on this page, it means the full finance function delivered as an ongoing service by one team.
